threads.body: [General] Preserve the read-only collection contract here. The previous implementation returned an unmodifiable structured list, but `collect(toList())` exposes a mutable `ArrayList`; consumers can now alter this configuration view, and this also violates the repository convention that collections exposed outside a class are unmodifiable.

replies.body: Good catch — fixed in b817897dab, with an assertion added so the read-only contract is pinned.

threads.body:
javadoc of `getBoolean` says that 
> Implementations should use the same rules as {@link Boolean#parseBoolean(String)} for handling the values.

`Boolean#parseBoolean` is implemented as `return "true".equalsIgnoreCase(s);`

replies.body: Thanks — switched to `Boolean.parseBoolean` in f0261a606c, for lists too. That makes any non-`"true"` string a valid `false`, so I also flipped the `isBoolean("string_key_with_env_quoted")` assertion in `DeclarativeConfigTest` (added with the 1.67 bump) to match the contract.

javadoc says that
> If the underlying config property is {@link Long}, it is converted to {@link Integer} with {@link Long#intValue()} which may result in loss of precision.

based on that the range check shouldn't be necessary.

replies.body: Agreed — removed the range check in f0261a606c; a `Long` is now narrowed with `Long.intValue()` as documented.

threads.body:
[P2] [Config] String-to-int conversion now silently wraps out-of-range values.

Routing every value through `getLong()` before narrowing means a Spring-resolved String `"4294967296"` now produces `getInt() == 0` and `isInt() == true`. Previously, `Integer.parseInt()` rejected it, allowing the configured default to apply. The SDK Javadoc permits narrowing an underlying `Long`, but this also narrows Strings that are not valid integers.

Please delegate native integer/Long reads to `delegate.getInt()` and retain `Integer.parseInt()` for Strings. Add positive and negative String-overflow cases alongside the existing native-Long test.

replies.body: Right — I applied the Long narrowing too broadly. Fixed in 5f1f90fa52: native `Integer`/`Long` go through `delegate.getInt()`, Strings still use `Integer.parseInt()`. Added `"2147483648"` / `"-2147483649"` (null, `isInt` false) plus the `MAX_VALUE` / `MIN_VALUE` boundaries next to the native-Long case.

threads.body:
[P2] [Config] Stringifying list elements turns native numbers into booleans.

This discards every scalar list element's original type. Reading `[true, 42, false]` as a Boolean list now returns `[true, false, false]`; previously, the numeric element was dropped. A numeric-only list now returns false entries instead of `null`, preventing default-list fallback. This affects typed values supplied by declarative model customizers and disagrees with the scalar getter, which still rejects numeric-to-Boolean conversion.

Please preserve original element types for typed-list conversion and apply `Boolean.parseBoolean()` only to originally String-valued elements. Add coverage for mixed Boolean/numeric lists and numeric-only lists.

replies.body: Agreed, stringifying lost the element types. Fixed in 5f1f90fa52: the decorator keeps the values it was created from and `getScalarList` converts each element with the same rules as the scalar getters, so `Boolean.parseBoolean` applies only to String elements. Added `[true, 42, false]` → `[true, false]` and `[1, 2]` → `null`.
